## Design

### 2026-11-01: I began week 4 by thinking about what I should make. I looked through google, YouTube, and even asked AI. Finally, I decided to make myself a device that would tell me what the cat wanted to eat. Part

**7.5h**

I began week 4 by thinking about what I should make. I looked through google, YouTube, and even asked AI. Finally, I decided to make myself a device that would tell me what the cat wanted to eat. Part of the inspiration came from my cats who would always make it known that they were hungry which was a little annoying. To make it fun, I settled on a device that when a button is clicked, the LED would turn on, signaling to me what type of food they want. It could be either wet food, dry food, or treats. I started working on it towards the end of the day. Since this was my second time using KiCad, I had AI help me along this journey in guiding me to understand the variety of tools this software had. It was completely different from traditional 3D Cad. The rest of the time was spent experimenting until I had what seemed like a rough schematic.

### 2026-11-01: On the next day, I ran the DRC after I double checked the schematic before I moved on. There were I believe 30+ errors with the schematic, so I had to find out why. Turns out I needed to block the oth

**8.75h**

On the next day, I ran the DRC after I double checked the schematic before I moved on. There were I believe 30+ errors with the schematic, so I had to find out why. Turns out I needed to block the other pins. Then, I had to add a power-flag for one of the GND symbols. Once that was all done, I moved on to the footprints where I settled on what type of LED I would use, what type of switch I would use, and the J1 and J2. I used tactile switch for the buttons which were small, but I'll probably glue cardboard or 3D print something to make the button bigger. The footprint was the biggest challenge because I had to decide on what type of ESP I would use that had 30 pins with 15 on each side. I settled on one of the dev kits. After finally finishing the footprint, I updated it into the PCB editor only to return and change some of the footprints.

### 2026-11-01: The final stretch: I just did all the journals on the last day  (sorry about that)

**7h**

The final stretch: I just did all the journals on the last day  (sorry about that)
After finishing the PCB layout, I added the "E.cut" thing around my device. I planned to have 5mm margins, so I changed it a little and then I started wiring. I began with the first layer where I routed the switches together and some of the ESP connectors. I then worked on the second layer where most of the work was done. In general, it was pretty much smooth sailing from there. I spent a considerate amount of time just writing text on it, but I finally decided to keep it simple. I was pretty content with the 3D model given the fact that it was my first time doing this type of project without much guidance. I exported the model using the plugin I installed in week 3's project and loaded it in into the JLCPCB to calculate the price. All in all, this was a learning experience, and I probably could've done better with the finish and obviously the time management. Definitely a cool skill set to have. Oh, and also, I had to ensure that the ESP was actually able to fit between the connectors
